what_it_does: Smart clothing systems need tiny processors woven directly into fabric. This paper describes kNOT (Network-on-Textiles), which integrates two miniaturized chips directly into braided yarns. The main chip is a computer-on-chip (SoC—System on a Chip) just 0.6×2.15mm in size, embedded in yarn with built-in memory and flexible connections. A second specialized chip enables multi-device communication using only 3 wires instead of the usual many. Rather than soldering chips onto bulky circuit boards, this work laser-ablates selective spots in yarn and solders chips directly to it, making the textile wearable, flexible, and truly integrated.
